entries.text: Allah's Name to commence with, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Noon. (This is an individual letter of the Arabic alphabet; Allah and His Messenger know its exact meaning.) By the oath of the pen and of what it has written.
With the Benevolence of your Lord, (O Beloved) you are not insane.
And definitely for you is everlasting reward.
And (O Beloved), your (excellent) character is undoubtedly of a superb standard.
So, very soon you (O Beloved) will see and they too will see.
That who amongst you was insane.
Indeed, your Lord knows well those who have strayed from His path, and He knows well those who are upon the path (of guidance).
Therefore, do not listen to those who belie.
They are wishing this that in some way you may soften (i.e. compromise on religious issues) so they too might soften their stand.
And do not listen to any excessive oath-monger, disgraceful person (i.e. Waleed Bin Mugheerah).
The excessive taunter going about excessively slandering.
The excessive hinderer of goodness; transgressor; sinner.
With immoral character; besides all that, (he is) of an illegitimate birth.
Because he has some wealth and sons.
When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'These are the stories of the earlier people.'
We will soon brand him over his pig-like snout.
We have indeed tested them (i.e. the people of Makkah) the way We had tested the ones of that garden when they swore an oath that they would definitely cut its crop in the morning.
And (they) did not say, 'If Allah wills.'
So, a twister (i.e. severe storm) from your Lord completed its round (destroying the harvest) whilst they were sleeping.
So, in the morning it became like a destroyed fruit garden.
Then, they called out to each other at daybreak.
That 'Go to your farms in the early morning, if you want to pluck (fruit).'
So, they walked while whispering to one another.
That 'Today, no needy person should enter your garden at all.'
And they proceeded early in the morning, assuming they have power over their intention (to prevent the poor taking fruits therefrom).
Then when they saw it (i.e. the devastated garden), they said, 'We have indeed strayed.'
'Rather, we have become ill-fated.'
The most reasonable amongst them said, 'Did I not tell you that why do you not glorify (Allah)?'
They said, 'Glory be to our Lord; indeed, we were unjust.'
Now, one approached the other (while) blaming.
They said, 'Woe to us! Indeed, we were rebellious.'
'Hopefully, our Lord may give us a better replacement (i.e. garden) than this; we turn towards our Lord.'
Such is the punishment; and indeed, the punishment of the Hereafter is the greatest, how good (it would have been for them) if they knew.
Indeed, for the pious ones with their Lord are Gardens of Bliss.
Should We make the Muslims equal to the criminals (in treatment)?
What is the matter with you? How (unwisely) do you judge?
Is there a (Divine) Book for you from which you read?
That for you therein is (such writing) what you choose?
Or do you have some oaths (binding) upon Us, stretching until the Day of Resurrection, that you will get whatever you claim?
You should ask them, who amongst them is a guarantor for that (claim)?
Or do they have partners (who may support them in their claim)? So, they should bring their partners, if they are truthful.
On the Day when a Shin will be exposed (the meaning of which only Allah knows) and they will be called to prostrate, so they will be unable to do so.
With lowered eyes, humiliation will be overcoming them; and indeed, they used to be called in this world to prostrate whilst they were healthy.
Therefore, the one who belies this discourse (i.e. the Qur'aan), leave him to Me; it is close that We will gradually take them from where they know not.
And I will give them respite; indeed, My hidden plan is very solid.
Or is it that you (O Beloved) ask for compensation from them, that they are burdened with the penalty?
Or that they possess the (knowledge of the) unseen; that (with it) they are writing it down (that they are successful)?
Therefore, wait for the command of your Lord, and do not be like the one associated with the fish (i.e. the Prophet Yunus) who called (upon his Lord) in a state when he was in distress.
Had the favour of his Lord not reached in order to take care of him, so he would have certainly been thrown onto the bare shore, condemned (by his people).
His Lord henceforth chose him and made him amongst those who deserve His special closeness.
And the disbelievers definitely seem as if they would make you fall down by casting their evil eyes when they hear the Qur'aan, and they say, 'This (Prophet Muhammad) is far from intelligence.'
And that (i.e. the Qur'aan or the Beloved Prophet) is not but advice to all the worlds.
